correctness.rationale: The frozen geometry sentence excluded collinearity without a degree restriction, false for two distinct points on an affine line, and was imprecise about the sign in the reciprocal relation. The complete repaired RESULT gives the degree-two roots explicitly, proves noncollinearity for n≥3, and states the negative-reciprocal relation. Re-audit: Poisson/Parseval gives twice the sum of power-sum squares; the diagonal terms diverge at the circle while the real off-diagonal terms each exceed −1/2. Newton coordinates give the feasible comparison with S_2 through S_n zero and force every global minimizer into the feasible convex slice where the tail Hessian is small. Normal convergence of the complexified tail justifies the derivatives and positive Hessian there. From the truncated logarithm S_{n+1} is (n+1) times the first omitted coefficient of the exponential. Its baseline and differentiated baseline give the stated sign and factorial coefficient in Wirtinger stationarity; uniform Cauchy bounds after rescaling S_k/s^k give a geometric remainder starting at m=n+2, and the refinement S_k/s^k=O(|s|²) gives the other remainder of the same order. Squaring verifies the variance defect with its factor of 2. The limiting reversed polynomial equals z^n T_n(−1/z); T_n and T_n' cannot share a root. Simple-root perturbation yields order |s|³ for the zeros. For n≥3 the second limiting power sum forces an affine line, if any, to be purely imaginary in direction, whereupon the real part of the third sum is −2/n² instead of zero.
residual_risks: Constants and locality threshold are only for fixed n; no uniformity across degrees or classification at large |s|.
Finite diagnostics in the package are not the all-degree proof.

value.rationale: Fixing the first Fourier coefficient is a natural design constraint on angular speed. A sharp all-degree next term isolates the obstruction left by the finite number of movable zeros; global uniqueness and the factorial scale with limiting root geometry are substantially stronger than a lower bound from this coefficient alone.
residual_risks: The result solves the fixed-degree small-centroid regime only; the comparison does not provide a full-size or degree-uniform design rule.
